FILES

Drop art here .png, .xml, level .json, .zip

Props and the title graphic draw from the images you load. A .zip keeps their folder paths, so storymenu/props/bf.png lands under that name.

SONGS

The order here is the order they play. The first song decides which difficulties the level offers.

PROPS

0

Each prop sits 320px further right than the one before it, on top of its own offset. Order is position.

100%
nothing selected

SELECTED PROP

Nothing selected. Add a prop, or click one in the preview.

The image path under your mod's images folder, without the extension.

 

Beats between bops. 1 is every beat, 2 every other. Steps of 0.25.

Pixel turns off smoothing and multiplies the scale by 6, the way the game does.

Left blank the prop just dances on one frame. Name an animation and it plays that instead.

ANIMATIONS

0

A prop with no animations is a still image. Add one and it reads the art as a Sparrow sheet instead.

The game looks for idle to dance, and confirm when the level is picked.

The frame name in the XML, without its numbering.

LEVEL

The file name, and how a song's playData refers to this level.

Shown in the top corner of the story menu.

The graphic in the scrolling list of levels.

The game reads a leading # as a colour and anything else as an image path.

Ticked, the level is left out of the story menu entirely. Its songs still show up in Freeplay.

FREEPLAY CAPSULE

Optional. The text stamped on this level's songs in Freeplay. Leave it blank and the game spaces out the level id instead, and the block is left out of the file.

Preview only — the title comes from the song's own metadata. It is here so you can see how long a name fits before it starts scrolling.

CAPSULE ICON

Drop an icon here its .png, and .xml if it animates

The pixel icon on the capsule. It belongs to the song, not the level — the game loads images/freeplay/icons/<songCharacter>pixel.png.

 

The game adds every icon animation at 10, hardcoded. Changing it here only changes the preview.

The icon scales by 2 about this point, which is what slides it left of the title. The game uses 100 for every character but two.

LEVEL JSON

Paste it into data/levels/<id>.json.
